author: CC
prose: The artifact journal's _append opens .artifact-journal.jsonl a+, flocks, reads the whole file, then writes the new line. A git stash/checkout/rebase in the same tree replaces the file at that path (a new inode) and ignores the flock, so a line written in that window lands in the orphaned inode and is lost, while the record the door wrote a moment earlier rides the stash back. Measured 2026-11-13: f695fac922cd's PROVEME cursor write (cert f695fac922cd-PROVEME-20261113T163007Z-80cd) lost its journal line inside a batch's pull --rebase --autostash window in the live commons, and every commons commit then refused with 'changed around the door'; reproduced in a scratch repo by repro_inode.py (inode replaced: True; state s1 kept; journal line missing). The append should notice the handle no longer names the file at the path and land the line in the file that is there.
